title: 9 Best Spice Farm Tours in Zanzibar
description: The best spice farm tours in Zanzibar — curated from Reddit reviews. From organic farms to cooking-class combos, explore cloves, vanilla, cinnamon & more. Interactive map included.

places.name: Tangawizi Spice Farm

redditQuotes.text: At Tangawizi spice farm we saw spice plants for 1.5 hours. We tasted tropical fruits as well. We enjoyed a lot! I recommend it.
Spice Farms that I heard from other travellers we met that are equally as good: Hakuna Matata Farm, Tangawizi Spice Farm, Kidichi Spice Farm.

places.verdict: The most consistently recommended farm name across reviews.

comparison.best for: Organic Farm in Near Stone Town, central Zanzibar with a $15–$25/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.6★ from 638 Google reviews · Organic Farm · Near Stone Town, central Zanzibar
comparison.why it made the list: The most consistently recommended farm name across reviews. Close to Stone Town, well-organized, and the guides are enthusiastic without being pushy. A solid default choice if you want the classic spice tour experience.

places.insiderTip: The most consistently recommended farm name across reviews. Close to Stone Town, well-organized, and the guides are enthusiastic without being pushy. A solid default choice if you want the classic spice tour experience.

places.name: Kizimbani Spice Farm

redditQuotes.text: The Zanzibar Spice Tour proceeds to the Kizimbani Village in the Central District, where the first spices were planted by the first Arab sultan.
Kizimbani spice farm — it's top rated.

places.verdict: If history matters to you, Kizimbani is the farm to visit.

comparison.best for: Historic Plantation in Kizimbani Village, central Zanzibar with a $15–$20/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ from 46 Google reviews · Historic Plantation · Kizimbani Village, central Zanzibar
comparison.why it made the list: If history matters to you, Kizimbani is the farm to visit. It's where Zanzibar's spice story literally began. The plantations feel more authentic and less "tourist showcase" than some competitors. The deeper historical context gives this tour an edge.

places.name: Kidichi Spice Farm & Persian Baths
places.address: Kidichi Village, north of Stone Town

redditQuotes.text: The Spice Tour begins at Kidichi Village to visit the Persian Baths built by the first sultan of Zanzibar.
Very interesting, just don't buy anything — the souvenir prices at the end are inflated. But the tour itself is great.

places.verdict: The two-for-one combo of spices + Persian baths makes this the best value outing.

comparison.best for: Historic Site in Kidichi Village, north of Stone Town with a $15–$25/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.9★ from 294 Google reviews · Historic Site · Kidichi Village, north of Stone Town
comparison.why it made the list: The two-for-one combo of spices + Persian baths makes this the best value outing. The baths alone are worth a detour. Just know that the souvenir shop at the end will be pushy — politely decline and you'll be fine.

places.name: Zanzibar Organic Spice Farm

redditQuotes.text: I visited an organic spice farm and was surprised by how fun and educational it was! They let you touch, smell, and even taste the spices.
We took a tour to the spice farm with a local guide Ibrahim. Amazing experience in Zanzibar. Lots of fun and amazing smells. A real experience not to be missed.

places.verdict: If you care about sustainable tourism, this is your farm.

comparison.best for: Certified Organic in Central Zanzibar, near Masingini Forest with a $25–$45/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.7★ from 34 Google reviews · Certified Organic · Central Zanzibar, near Masingini Forest
comparison.why it made the list: If you care about sustainable tourism, this is your farm. The organic certification is real, not just marketing. Slightly pricier but you're supporting actual sustainable farming. The cooking class add-on is worth it.

places.insiderTip: If you care about sustainable tourism, this is your farm. The organic certification is real, not just marketing. Slightly pricier but you're supporting actual sustainable farming. The cooking class add-on is worth it.

places.name: Hakuna Matata Spice Farm

redditQuotes.text: Hakuna Matata Farm, Tangawizi Spice Farm, Kidichi Spice Farm — all equally as good. We visited Hakuna Matata and loved the personal touch.

places.verdict: The name is cheesy (yes, it means "no worries") but the experience is genuine.

comparison.best for: Family-Run in Near Masingini Forest, central Zanzibar with a $15–$20/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ from 665 Google reviews · Family-Run · Near Masingini Forest, central Zanzibar
comparison.why it made the list: The name is cheesy (yes, it means "no worries") but the experience is genuine. Smaller groups, more personal interaction with the guides, and less of a conveyor-belt feel than some of the bigger operations. Good for families with kids.

places.name: Azusa Spice Farm & Cooking Class
places.address: Stone Town departure, Darajani Market + spice farm

redditQuotes.text: After buying goods at the market, visit of a spice farm. Azusa Spice Farm. Then cooking a 4 plates meal. Marvelous with a lot of tips to prepare rice pilau. The lady who gave the course was exceptional.

places.verdict: The best premium option if you want more than just looking at plants.

comparison.best for: Cooking Class in Stone Town departure, Darajani Market + spice farm with a $45–$60/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.8★ from 103 Google reviews · Cooking Class · Stone Town departure, Darajani Market + spice farm
comparison.why it made the list: The best premium option if you want more than just looking at plants. The market-to-farm-to-kitchen journey gives real context to Zanzibar's food culture. You'll walk away knowing how to make pilau rice — and that alone is worth the price.

places.name: Masingini Forest Spice Farms
places.address: Masingini Forest, 20 min from Stone Town

redditQuotes.text: It's a simple, no stress, 3 hour tour that will take you to the spice plantations in the Masingini Forest. The tour entails a guide taking you around the spice farm.
I've been on two spice tours already and can say that they are all the same but all equally as interesting.

places.verdict: The honest truth: most basic spice tours from Stone Town end up at one of the Masingini farms.

redditQuotes.text: Zanzibar Bahama spice farm, are you in Zanzibar now?

places.verdict: If you're on a tight budget and arranged your own transport (dala-dala or taxi), visiting a smaller farm like Bahama directly can save you $10-15 over booking through a tour agency.

places.name: Mtende Spice & Herb Garden

redditQuotes.text: One of the most underrated experiences in Zanzibar is exploring the local villages and engaging in cultural tours like the Zanzibar spice farm visits — the ones away from the main tourist areas are the best.

comparison.best for: Medicinal Herbs in Southeast Zanzibar, near Mtende with a $15–$25/person spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ from 379 Google reviews · Medicinal Herbs · Southeast Zanzibar, near Mtende
comparison.why it made the list: The off-the-beaten-path pick. If you're staying on the east coast near Paje or Jambiani, Mtende is much closer than the Stone Town farms. The medicinal herb angle gives it a unique dimension — you won't just see cinnamon and cloves, you'll learn about centuries-old healing traditions.
